newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai car makers to raise prices as baht tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Thai car makers to raise prices as baht tumbles.

text.p: Auto makers in Thailand plan to raise prices of locally-assembled passenger cars and commercial vehicles as costs of imported car parts have increased following the baht's recent tumble, industry source said on Monday.

"Our cost of import parts has been rising significantly as result of the baht's depreciation. There must be some price adjustment for new car models," said Surapong Paisitpatnapong, spokesman for the Thai Automotive Industry Association.
He told Reuters that the exact increase had not yet been determined as the industry was still tracking fluctuations in the baht.
The currency has depreciated by around 15 percent since July 2, when it was released from a 13-year peg to a trade-weighted basket of currencies, dominated by the dollar into a managed float system.
"Some manufacturers of car parts are demanding price rises. The price hike of assembled cars is inevitable, but we have to work out the exact amount later," Surpong said.
Most of the auto parts are imported from Japan.
Any price increase, coupled with Thailand's worst economic downturn in over a decade, would have adverse affects on car sales this year, he added.
Sales this year are now expected to fall to 460,000 compared with an earlier forecast of 600,000, he said.
Car prices are controlled by the government and currently are already below the maximum allowed. There was no need for the industry to seek government approval to raise car prices, Surapong added.
